ui_bugs.issue: ChartFrame gating (mount ResponsiveContainer only when wrapper clientWidth>0) STILL emits 4x 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' warnings. Root cause: even after the wrapper is measured, Recharts ResponsiveContainer's own internal state initializes as {containerWidth:-1, containerHeight:-1} and its render logs the warning synchronously BEFORE its internal ResizeObserver reports a size. Gating the parent width does not stop Recharts's own first-tick warning.
ui_bugs.priority: LOW (cosmetic console noise; charts render fine)

action_items: The ChartFrame fix does NOT stop the warnings. Recharts ResponsiveContainer logs the warning from its OWN render on mount regardless of parent size. Real fixes: (a) drop ResponsiveContainer entirely, measure wrapper via ResizeObserver and pass numeric width/height props directly to <BarChart>/<PieChart>; (b) upgrade recharts to a version where the warning is removed/gated; (c) suppress the warning by wrapping console.warn (not recommended); (d) accept as cosmetic-only — it does not affect functionality.

Recommended: replace ChartFrame's `ready` gate with a `{width, height}` state pair set from ResizeObserver, and render <BarChart width={width} height={height} ...> and <PieChart width={width} height={height} ...> directly (no ResponsiveContainer). This will fully eliminate the warning.
critical_code_review_comments: ChartFrame.jsx assumption is incorrect: gating ResponsiveContainer mount on wrapper clientWidth>0 does NOT prevent Recharts's internal warning because Recharts logs during its own first render tick (containerWidth/Height start at -1 in its state). The only reliable way is to bypass ResponsiveContainer and pass numeric width/height to the chart components directly.

Minor: ChartFrame spreads `...rest` (including `data-testid`) onto the outer <div>, which is fine, but the ResponsiveContainer inside still initializes with width=-1 and warns before its own observer fires.

rca of the issue: Recharts <ResponsiveContainer width='100%' height='100%'> initializes its internal state with containerWidth=-1, containerHeight=-1 and executes a console.warn during its FIRST render tick before its internal ResizeObserver callback runs. Gating the PARENT wrapper's mount on clientWidth>0 (as ChartFrame does) merely delays when ResponsiveContainer mounts but does NOT change ResponsiveContainer's own initial internal state — the warning fires on ResponsiveContainer's first render regardless. Mitigation: bypass ResponsiveContainer entirely; measure the wrapper (ResizeObserver) and pass numeric width/height props to <BarChart>/<PieChart> directly.
